assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of record accuracy and stability with strontium, removed the Doppler and recoil limits by trapping many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime. They have taken timekeeping to about the 1e-18 level and underpin relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches. From an atomic-physics view this is a clean, original idea with an exceptionally sharp realisation.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the magic-wavelength proposal and the first demonstrations; Ye's group brought the clocks to the leading accuracy and stability and connected them to frequency combs and metrology. Two names give a coherent configuration. The ion-clock and frequency-comb contributions are already recognised by the 2005 and 2012 prizes, so credit separation is relatively clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent groups have confirmed the approach, comparisons between clocks across continents exist, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether others such as Pierre Lemonde or Hidetoshi Katori's early collaborators deserve comparable credit is not resolved in the supplied credit list.
Close overlap with the thorium-229 nuclear clock candidate and with ion-clock work recognised earlier could be seen as incremental by some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of a Higgs-like boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and was a monumental measurement. The theory was recognised in 2013; the experimental discovery itself is a landmark of lasting importance with continuing precision programmes.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the founding proposers and leaders of ATLAS and CMS. This is a natural configuration but is a leadership-based attribution for collaborations of thousands, and the decisive analysis contributions are diffuse. I am uncertain whether the committee would accept this basis.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the discovery was independently established by two experiments and the properties are now measured to about 10 percent in several couplings.
uncertainties: Attribution to collaboration leaders rather than discrete individual discoveries may be contentious.
Whether the 2013 prize is seen as having already covered the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: AdS/CFT is one of the most influential theoretical ideas of the last decades, linking quantum gravity and gauge theory and providing tools used in strongly coupled systems and black hole information. Its originality and conceptual reach are outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena made the conjecture; Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten gave the operational dictionary. The supplied names also include 't Hooft and Susskind for holography, so allocation is genuinely difficult. I propose three but acknowledge the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mathematically and theoretically very well supported, but there is no direct experimental confirmation as a statement about nature, which is a significant maturity concern for a physics prize.
uncertainties: No empirical test of the duality as a description of physical gravity.
Credit overlap among five credited names and exclusion of Klebanov and Gubser from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave coherence into a precision instrument, with gravimeters, gradiometers, measurements of constants such as the fine-structure constant and tests of the equivalence principle. This is an area I know well in terms of the underlying atomic physics, and the importance is clear.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard produced the early atom interferometer and Bordé the theoretical treatment of the Ramsey-Bordé interferometer; Kasevich demonstrated the precision inertial sensors. Chu's and Ramsey's related contributions were recognised earlier, which complicates a clean boundary, but the three names form a plausible set.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with commercial gravimeters, large-baseline experiments and many confirming groups; some applications such as gravitational-wave detection remain prospective.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1997 and 1989 prizes about laser cooling and separated oscillatory fields makes novelty relative to those awards arguable.
Relative weight of Bordé's theory versus experimental demonstrations by others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light moved from a quantum-optics concept to a deployed tool, now improving LIGO and Virgo sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit. Caves supplied the key proposal, and the first experimental squeezing and later low-frequency frequency-dependent squeezing are significant.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed the interferometer application, Kimble's group made the first observation of squeezed states, and Schnabel developed the squeezed-light sources for gravitational-wave detectors. Mavalvala and others also contributed substantially, so the three-name limit forces a difficult choice, and Slusher's contribution to the first observation is not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed in several detectors, with a direct link to a previously recognised discovery.
uncertainties: Contested allocation of credit among theory, first experiments and detector implementation.
The credited list is four names and I can select at most three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution is a foundational application of quantum mechanics to secure communication, with satellite and fibre implementations. It is conceptually important as a link between foundations and information.
assessment.attribution: BB84 was by Bennett and Brassard, and Ekert's E91 gave an entanglement-based approach. I propose Bennett and Brassard as the clearest originators, but Ekert's independent proposal is a real competing claim.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are well established, though practical security against implementation attacks remains an active field and deployment is limited, so recognition may be somewhat early for physical impact.
uncertainties: Ekert's role compared with Bennett and Brassard.
Gap between theoretical security and device-level security.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical-lattice quantum simulation, from the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition through single-site resolution, realised controllable many-body Hamiltonians and has become a main platform of quantum science. Strongly related to my atomic-physics background, the scientific value is high.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard-model implementation; Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch demonstrated the Mott transition; Esslinger's fermionic experiments and Bloch's later work also matter. Allocation among four credited names is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a platform with many confirming groups, although the most consequential quantum-advantage-style results for simulation are still emerging.
uncertainties: Overlap with the trapped-ion and cold-atom quantum computing candidate and with the 2001 and 2012 recognitions of atom cooling and quantum control.
Selection among Bloch, Esslinger, Greiner and Zoller is ambiguous.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a field of moire quantum materials with tunable correlated insulators and superconductivity. The theory predicted flat bands and the experiments demonstrated them, giving a rapid and unusually strong theory-experiment pairing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic-angle flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated insulator and superconductivity. Cao and others in the experiment are not among the credited names, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the pairing mechanism and the interpretation of the correlated states are not settled, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Credit of the experimental team beyond the senior author is not represented.
